name: Interview Prep Desk - interview agent spec
about: Single source of truth for the mock-interview agent. The page reads its prompts from this file; a future agent built on the Claude API should load the same file so scoring stays consistent. Question bank: questions.json (same folder).

shape.i: stable question id (string). Bank ids start with 'r', user-added ids start with 'u'
shape.t: technology key: react | javascript | html | css | typescript | web
shape.c: concept key (see concepts in the page, e.g. hooks_adv, redux, router)
shape.s: sources: ib | gfg | gfe | sj | bfe | gfeq | feih | h5bp | ipd (written by Claude) | me (added by you)
shape.k: type: t (theory) | c (coding) | o (predict the output) | d (system design)
shape.code: optional code snippet that belongs to the question
shape.pg: optional id of a verified playground challenge for this question (see playground.json)

questionBank.userAddedQuestions: stored in the page database, collection 'custom', same shape plus cn (concept display name) and at (created timestamp)

answers.shape: {v, by, answers:{<questionId>:{a, p[], c?, lang?, f}}}
answers.note: One original reference answer per question in questions.json (a = answer, p = key points, c = code, f = likely follow-up). Answers saved on the page (db collection 'answers') take precedence. The evaluator passes a = + p as {{reference}}.

progress/{questionId}.n: string - the user's own answer notes
progress/{questionId}.ls: number 0-10 - last interview score for this question
progress/{questionId}.na: number - how many times it has been asked in interviews

interviews/{sessionId}.summary: summary object (see summary.output) plus overall (0-10 average) and byConcept {conceptKey: {avg, n}}

selection.rule: Pick questions from the chosen technology, concepts and level. Prefer questions never asked (na missing), then questions with a low last score (ls < 6), then not-yet-revised ones; shuffle within each group; at most 3 questions from one concept when several concepts are chosen.

evaluation.followUpBlock:
The interviewer then asked a follow-up question.
Follow-up: {{followUp}}
Candidate's follow-up answer:
"""
{{followUpAnswer}}
"""
Score the original answer and the follow-up answer together as one response.
evaluation.followUpRuleFirst: one natural follow-up question an interviewer would ask next to probe deeper into this answer, or "" if the answer scored 3 or below
evaluation.followUpRuleFinal: always "" (the follow-up has already been asked)
evaluation.referenceBlock:
Reference notes for the grader (a model answer prepared for this question; use it to check accuracy and coverage, but accept other correct approaches and do not require its exact wording):
"""
{{reference}}
"""

summary.prompt:
You are a senior frontend interviewer writing feedback after a mock {{tech}} interview. Here is each question with its concept, score out of 10 and the points the candidate missed:

{{itemsBlock}}

Overall average: {{overall}}/10.

Reply with only this JSON object:
{"headline":"...","strengths":["..."],"focus":[{"concept":"...","why":"..."}],"plan":["..."]}
- headline: one sentence verdict on how interview-ready the candidate is for these topics
- strengths: up to 3 things they showed they know well
- focus: up to 3 concepts to study next, each with one sentence on what exactly to work on (use the concept names given above)
- plan: 3 concrete next study steps, each one sentence

selfScoring.about: Used when AI scoring is unavailable. The candidate rates themselves after seeing the question again.

notes: Keep the Claude API key on a server you control (for example a small serverless function). Never put it inside this page or any web page: anyone who can open the page could read it.

The agent loads questions.json plus the user's custom questions, selects questions with the selection rule, asks them one at a time, and calls Claude with evaluation.prompt for each answer, then summary.prompt at the end.
Store results in the interviews/{sessionId} shape above so the page's history and reports can show them.

kinds.code: fill-the-blanks + write-the-code with tests (JavaScript, runs in a Web Worker)
kinds.output: guess the output; answer is the exact console output

fill.answers: tokens for each blank in order

write.tests: [{name, run}] where run is an async function body using expect(x).toBe(y) / toEqual(y) / toThrow() and await wait(ms)

storage.pg/{challengeId}: {f: fill solved, w: tests passed, o: right|wrong}
storage.gen/{questionId}: AI-made challenge in the same shape, verified by running before it is shown

playground.aiGeneration: For a coding question without a ready-made challenge, the page asks Claude for a challenge in the shape above, runs the solution against the tests and keeps only passing tests; for output puzzles it runs the code and corrects the answer to the real output.

sources.pendingLinks: links/{id}: {url, note, at} saved on the Sources page for later coverage
